2.0.2 moves the search database to Weaviate 1.39.14. It changes no API, no configuration and no stored data. Upgrade any 2.0.x installation to it.
- **Safer restarts.** A crash right after a shutdown could leave a keyword-search file empty, and the database would then not start without a manual repair. Startup and shutdown are also faster.
1. Back up the search database volume.

- **Weaviate 1.39.13** replaces 1.39.10 as the search database. It rejects TLS certificate chains built on the eight leaked eMudhra intermediate certificates (CVE-2026-111943). Weaviate uses TLS for backups, OIDC and model modules.
1. Back up the search database volume, as before any database upgrade.
- **Search** recovers after a database restart, with its buffers restored and its hydration work bounded.

First stable release of the Tidbyt Enterprise flyby (64x32, Pixlet/Starlark): the original-series USS Enterprise sweeps across your display, drops out of warp for a phaser battle with a Klingon, or comes right at you.
On an original Tidbyt, a pushed animation plays about 1.4x slower than its 50 ms frame delay suggests, so the parts last roughly 10 s (Flyby), 12 s (Skirmish) and 9 s (Head-on). A pushed image ignores the settings form; the Part dropdown appears when the app runs from the community store.

Third release candidate of the Tidbyt Enterprise flyby (64x32, Pixlet/Starlark).
Measured on an original Tidbyt from a phone video: a pushed animation plays about 1.4x slower than its 50 ms frame delay suggests (roughly 14 frames per second), so the parts last about 10 s (Flyby), 12 s (Skirmish) and 9 s (Head-on) on the device. A pushed image is a fixed animation: it ignores the settings form and `show_full_animation`, which only apply to apps run from the community store.

Second release candidate of the Tidbyt Enterprise flyby (64x32, Pixlet/Starlark).
Release candidate: all views were checked in Pixlet previews, and the full show has run on a real Tidbyt. A pushed image is a fixed animation and ignores the scene settings and `show_full_animation`; those only apply when the app runs from the community store.

### Added
- Notes: Ctrl + click (Cmd + click on macOS) on a bullet's arrow expands or collapses it together with all its sub-bullets, on every level. A single Ctrl + Z takes it back.

### Changed
- Notes: focus mode shows the note as wide as the editor with the folder sidebar hidden, instead of a narrow reading column.

### Fixed
- Notes: right after reloading the page, focus mode started with the note at the very top instead of keeping it at the height it had in the workspace.

### Added
- Notes: "Copy link" in the note's ⋯ menu copies a link to the note. Clicking it opens the note in MindSift (in the installed app where the system allows it), also for everyone the note is shared with.
- Tasks and shopping lists: sort the list tabs by drag and drop. The order is your own (also for shared lists) and is used in the phone menu as well; new lists go to the end.
- Administration: redeemed and expired invites disappear from the list 30 days later; until then the row says when.
- Tasks

### Added
- MCP: notes, tasks and lists in tool results carry a `url` that opens them in the app (needs `BASE_URL`), so an assistant can link to what it found. Links of the form `/?note=…`, `/?task=…` and `/?list=…` open the item after signing in.

### Fixed
- MCP: `create_note` no longer creates an empty note when a model sends plain text. Every line becomes a bullet, content sent as a list of strings or with doubly escaped line breaks works too, and if nothing usable is left the result says so inste
